headlines.article_text: Musk claims Ukraine violated Starlink service agreement Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said the company restricted Ukraine's access to its high-speed technology because Kyiv violated Starlink's terms of service. Ukraine’s Defense Ministry said Starlink and Starshield connectivity is again restored on equipment moving above 400 km/h (249 mph). Ukrainian officials said the restrictions disrupted some drone operations and weakened the country’s ability to respond to Russian attacks. In this article SPCX SPCX Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT SpaceX CEO Elon Musk looks on as President Donald Trump speaks to the press after a meeting with technology executives about artificial intelligence at the White House in Washington, Sept. 29, 2026. Kent Nishimura | AFP | Getty Images SpaceX CEO Elon Musk on Saturday said the company restricted Ukraine's access to its high-speed technology because Kyiv violated Starlink's terms of service. In a post on X , Musk said: "Ukraine military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week." He added: "SpaceX has done more to defend Ukraine than any private company on Earth BY FAR." Ukraine officials said earlier in the day that SpaceX's Starlink and Starshield satellite communication systems had restored high-speed service, a day after they said the service remained throttled. Ukrainian official said the service disruption left the country vulnerable to Russian attacks. "The monitoring systems of the Ministry of Defense of Ukraine officially record the restoration of the speed of Starlink/Starshield," it said in a statement . "The connection remains stable [while equipment is moving] at speeds over 400 km/h (249 miles per hour)." "Previously, monitoring systems recorded limitations in the operation of Starlink/Starshield. Now the speed indicators have been restored," the ministry added. Starlink is SpaceX's broader commercial satellite internet network, while Starshield is the company's government operations built on Starlink technology. Before Musk's announcement, confusion lingered over who ordered the high-speed service restrictions, with Musk initially claiming in a social media post the U.S. government was responsible, while President Donald Trump had said he had no knowledge of it. On Saturday, speaking to White House reporters in Florida, Trump confirmed a Wall Street Journal report this week that said he had asked Musk to ease the restrictions : "I have spoken to Elon Musk." SpaceX did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment. A soldier from a separate task rifle battalion of the National Police of Ukraine uses a smartphone to check signal quality while setting up a Starlink satellite communication network at a combat position in the Donetsk region, Ukraine, on October 16, 2026. Dmytro Smolienko | Nurphoto | Getty Images Since Oct. 14, Ukrainian officials have accused SpaceX of undermining the country's ability to defend itself by imposing speed limits on Starshield, the military-grade offering of its Starlink satellite internet service. Officials said any drone traveling above 100 mph lost its connection, disrupting some missions. Ukraine's Starshield terminals continued to experience problems on Friday, said Dmitri Alperovitch, chairman of the Silverado Policy Accelerator, a Washington, D.C., think tank focused on energy, defense tech and global trade. 'Things have become harder' Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in a Friday post on X that the restrictions on Starlink and Starshield "are still there," and added, "The speed has not been restored." He noted that the country is also waiting for the U.S. to deliver missile interceptors "that were already agreed on." "Things have become harder — partly because of the Starlink and Starshield policies and speed limits," Zelenskyy wrote. "But our frontline is still holding and I am proud of how strong our people are." Ukraine's Ministry of Defense said it continues to monitor the systems' operations. "This result is, above all, important for our front, for the military, the work of drones, logistics, and communications," Defense Minister Yevgeny Khmara said in the statement. Lawmakers in the U.S. from both parties have called for a formal probe into Musk and SpaceX over alleged unilateral changes the company made to its services in Ukraine. headlines.summary: A drug from Amgen could give patients with an aggressive form of lung cancer significantly more time to live when added to an immunotherapy from AstraZeneca.
headlines.article_text: Amgen's Imdelltra combo cuts risk of death by 58% in lung cancer Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points A drug from Amgen could give patients with a notoriously aggressive form of lung cancer significantly more time to live when added to an immunotherapy from AstraZeneca. Full results from a late-stage trial show that adding Amgen's Imdelltra to AstraZeneca's Imfinzi drug slashed the risk of death by 58% in patients with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer. Extensive-stage small cell lung cancer is a fast-growing disease that has spread beyond the lung where it began. In this article AMGN Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT The Amgen logo is displayed outside Amgen headquarters in Thousand Oaks, California, on May 17, 2023. Mario Tama | Getty Images A drug from Amgen could give patients with a notoriously aggressive form of lung cancer significantly more time to live when added to an immunotherapy from AstraZeneca , a study found. Full results from a late-stage trial released Saturday show that adding Amgen's immunotherapy Imdelltra to AstraZeneca's Imfinzi drug slashed the risk of death by 58% in patients with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer, a fast-growing disease that has spread beyond the lung where it began. The drug combination extended their median overall survival to 21.1 months compared with 12.7 months with AstraZeneca's drug alone, the trial found. That means half of patients in the group that took the combination regimen were alive for at least roughly 21 months. The trial tested the combo as a maintenance therapy in patients who received initial treatment with Imfinzi and chemotherapy, and whose cancer had not progressed. "I think there are moments in medicine when you see a piece of data that is so profound that it's going to transform the standard of care for patients, and I think, honestly, we're at that moment," said Dr. Paul Burton, Amgen's chief medical officer, in an interview. The combination "has the potential to take on one of the most aggressive cancers that we deal with today, and almost convert it into a chronic disease," he said, adding that "these data say that's a possibility." The results also suggest a greater commercial opportunity for Imdelltra, which posted $288 million in sales during the second quarter, up 115% year over year. The drug already generated $627 million in global sales in 2025 and appears to be on its way to becoming a blockbuster medicine, or hitting the $1 billion sales threshold. Small cell lung cancer remains difficult to treat because, even if chemotherapy initially works well for most patients, the disease often returns or progresses within months, said lead trial investigator Dr. Jacob Sands, who is the associate chief of the Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. He said immunotherapy has helped a small subset of patients achieve years of disease control, but most have not experienced similarly durable benefits, highlighting the need for better treatments. There are roughly 31,000 new small cell lung cancer cases in the U.S. each year, and an estimated 60% to 70% of those people are diagnosed with extensive-stage disease. Sands said the benefits in the trial were seen across subgroups of patients, including those whose cancer spread to the brain or liver. Disease that has spread to those organs is associated with poorer treatment outcomes. He added that with longer-term follow-up data on the patients, the 21-month figure "may evolve further and hopefully will substantially improve," similar to what Amgen saw in a Phase 1 trial on the immunotherapy combination. In that early-stage trial on a smaller number of patients, a long-term follow-up showed the benefit was sustained for years. Using Imdelltra earlier Amgen said the findings also suggest that using Imdelltra earlier in a patient's treatment could meaningfully alter the trajectory of the disease. Imdelltra is currently approved for patients whose small cell lung cancer has progressed while they are on, or after, platinum-based chemotherapy. Researchers specifically tested whether adding Imdelltra could help patients live longer than continuing Imfinzi alone, which is already approved as a first treatment for this type of lung cancer. Amgen said nearly 80% of patients who started taking both drugs were alive at one year compared with 53% receiving Imfinzi alone. Imdelltra's "big impact" on controlling the disease and ultimately how long people live highlights the importance of including it in first-line maintenance treatment, Sands said. That refers to ongoing therapy given after an initial heavy treatment, such as chemotherapy or surgery. Burton added that it positions Amgen's drug to be an "indispensable backbone therapy" for small cell lung cancer, regardless of the other immunotherapy that can be paired with it. Imdelltra binds to DLL3, a protein on cancer cells, and CD3, a protein on T cells, which are a type of immune cell that can kill cancer. By binding to both, Imdelltra brings T cells into close contact with tumor cells, helping the immune system destroy the cancer. Imfinzi, made by AstraZeneca, is an immunotherapy that blocks a protein called PD-L1, which cancer cells use to evade the immune system. The drugs work together in complementary ways: Imfinzi helps remove the brakes on the immune response, while Imdelltra brings T cells directly to cancer cells and helps activate them to attack the tumor. The study, which was presented at a major cancer meeting called the European Society for Medical Oncology Congress, did not test whether the combination was better than other first-line treatment approaches. Still, the findings suggest Amgen's drug could be another option offered to small cell lung cancer patients earlier in their treatment. Kate Brenan, a 44-year-old mother of two from Denver, sees that as a win on its own. She was diagnosed with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer in early January 2024. Brenan underwent six rounds of a common combination chemotherapy, followed by chest radiation and later whole-brain radiation after the cancer spread. In September 2024, she started Imdelltra and has had no evidence of disease ever since. "I think that it's remarkable how quickly things are changing in the world of small cancer treatment options," Brenan told CNBC, adding that Imdelltra potentially becoming an earlier treatment option "can only be a good thing for the patients moving forward, and I'm really excited about that." Around 200 firefighters and emergency workers near Berchtesgaden in Bavaria were battling the flames after the building, known as the Kehlsteinhaus, caught fire on Friday, police said.
